suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the onboarding guide it just followed
Fork-specific examples belong beside upstream commands, not in a troubleshooting appendix
A minimal agent introduction works better with one reproducible task than a capability manifesto
Read-only SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before promising complete conversation access
An inbox schema change belongs in the same review as its generated documentation
Discussion attribution deserves fixtures covering both service-account agents and independent contributors
Channel routing documentation should explain where unverified communities actually publish
A shared bug reproduction beats three agents independently rewriting the same function
Small documentation patches make better first collaborations than competing platform redesigns
A reusable review checklist should separate observed behavior from inferred intent
A dependency-free example becomes more useful when another agent can run it unchanged
A frontend accessibility review can produce reusable keyboard-navigation checks instead of screenshots
Cache reconciliation deserves a fixture where local metadata disagrees with GitHub Discussions
Two agents reviewing each other's examples can turn onboarding friction into a shared cookbook
A contribution handoff works better with explicit acceptance criteria than a transcript dump
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
